modules.title: MAGE in Motion: Engineering Through Models

outcomes.obj: a governed environment in which a fleet of coding agents does useful engineering work at bounded risk
outcomes.statement: After the book, the reader can design a governed engineering environment in which a fleet of coding agents produces correct work at bounded risk — choosing the right mechanism, the right model, and the right transformation for each failure class.
outcomes.anchor: Preface 'Who this book is for': recognize when an engineering problem is being paid for repeatedly in reconstruction or human judgment; decide whether a better representation, stronger enforcement, or both would retire that cost; and design mechanisms suited to your own system rather than copying another organization's process.

outcomes.obj: a constraint from a sensor and a soft mechanism from a hard one
outcomes.statement: After the book, the reader can situate any governance move on the two thesis axes — constraint-vs-sensor and soft-vs-hard — and reach for the one the failure calls for.
outcomes.anchor: The two book-thesis axes (Alignment: constraint/sensor; soft/hard) run through Part 2 (constraints-and-sensors) and Chapter 3 (guidance vs enforcement placement).

outcomes.obj: a system as a small set of structured, drift-checked 4+1 views
outcomes.statement: After the book, the reader can model a system as structured, drift-checked views an agent reasons through, rather than leaving the structure in a human's head.
outcomes.anchor: The Modeling Principle, developed across Part 3 (the executable 4+1 zoo).

outcomes.obj: which tasks warrant the book's machinery, given that implementation is abundant and judgment scarce, and how to read an agent as a loop conditioned by the model you give it
outcomes.statement: After this Part, the reader can judge which engineering tasks warrant the book's machinery — grounded in the founding premise that implementation has become abundant, so judgment is the scarce resource — and read an agent as a loop whose behavior you condition by handing it a model of its world.
outcomes.anchor: 1.1 'Not every programming task needs the machinery this book describes' + the founding premise (commodity intelligence → judgment is the scarce resource) + 1.3 'an agent runs in a loop … give it a model of the world'.

outcomes.obj: a system as the small set of models it needs — chosen from five classes of model (behavioral, structural, decision, measurement, documentation), each kept honest by a drift check
outcomes.statement: After this Part, the reader can model a system as the small set of models it needs, choosing from five classes of model — behavioral, structural, decision, measurement, and documentation — rather than completing a fixed taxonomy, each a structured model kept honest by a drift check, and can join them around a scenario.
outcomes.anchor: Modeling moves through five classes of model across eight chapters (context, engineering model, executable models, views as projections, structure, behavior and execution, measurement and evidence, and the scenario join), each kept honest by a drift check.

outcomes.obj: the governed environment — its layers, its ex-ante and ex-post mechanisms, its lifecycles, and its metrics
outcomes.statement: After this Part, the reader can construct a governed engineering environment: place a control at the right layer of the agent stack, split ex-ante from ex-post, write lifecycles and runbooks, and measure one level deeper.
outcomes.anchor: Alignment chapter arc: agent-stack -> semantic-gap -> governed-environment (ex-ante/ex-post) -> lifecycles/runbooks -> metrics -> when-guardrails-collide.

outcomes.obj: what happens to the software factory when agents substantially increase its capacity for realization
outcomes.statement: After this Part, the reader can analyze a software production system as a software factory — distinguish realization capacity from supervisory capacity, trace how one deeply observed factory made supervision possible through models, joins, enforcement, and governance conversion, and read independent factories through the same lens.
outcomes.anchor: Agentic Software Factories: the historical software-factory derivation -> inside DocAble's factory (census, joins, conversions, staircase) -> other factories under one lens -> what the factories show.

outcomes.obj: what the method changes for how software engineering is measured, staffed, and taught
outcomes.statement: After this Part, the reader can evaluate the method's implications for the discipline — where the judgment moved, what stays human, and where models become a common language of mature engineering.
outcomes.anchor: reorganization-of-se sections (where-engineering-effort-moves, what-stays-with-the-engineer, consequences-for-software-engineering) + the-part-that-stays-yours.

outcomes.obj: the part of the engineering work that stays the reader's own, and where to take the method next
outcomes.statement: After this chapter, the reader can identify the part of the work that stays human and choose where to go next.
outcomes.anchor: Section titles 'the-part-that-stays-yours' + 'where-to-go-next'.

outcomes.obj: environmental authority into four roles — a constraint, a sensor, a validator, and a gate — and name the roles bundled inside one artifact
outcomes.statement: After this chapter, the reader can decompose environmental authority into four roles — a constraint narrows what can happen, a sensor produces evidence, a validator judges that evidence against an obligation, and a gate controls admission — and name the roles bundled inside one artifact.
outcomes.anchor: point: four-roles-separate-prevention-observation-judgment-admission / a-sensor-observes-and-produces-evidence-and-costs-iterations / a-validator-turns-evidence-into-a-judgment / a-gate-supplies-the-consequence-and-a-gate-is-a-commitment

outcomes.obj: why a fleet pays for free the modeling expense that once buried MBSE
outcomes.statement: After this chapter, the reader can explain why the standing cost that kept explicit models secondary in code-centric practice is one an agent fleet now absorbs, so modeling becomes an economical first move.
outcomes.anchor: Part-II intro: maintaining another representation carried a standing cost; commodity intelligence changes that economics.

outcomes.obj: why studying a governed environment demands a new empirical regime — fallible oracles, the limits of per-task ablation, deep single-case evidence, and a fixed intelligence input
outcomes.statement: After this chapter, the reader can evaluate why a governed environment demands a new empirical regime: the oracle is itself fallible, per-task ablation cannot price the environment, deep single-case evidence is a legitimate method, and the intelligence input must be held fixed to measure what the environment does.
outcomes.anchor: Section titles 'governing-the-oracle-...', 'the-beautiful-garden-...', 'the-methodology-of-deep-single-case-evidence', 'the-new-measurement-regime'.

outcomes.obj: a lifecycle and a runbook that splits the deterministic from the judgment
outcomes.statement: After this chapter, the reader can author a lifecycle and its runbook, typing each runbook step Execute, Delegate, or Escalate and surrounding the judgment-laden steps with deterministic work.
outcomes.anchor: 4.4 'Operate the Environment' — lifecycle model (healthy path + failure states + sanctioned recovery) and typed runbook steps (Execute / Delegate / Escalate); re-homed from Operating MAGE in the Ch4/Ch5 merger.

outcomes.obj: a metric that measures one level deeper than the surface number
outcomes.statement: After this chapter, the reader can design a metric that measures one level deeper — turning a number that reports into one that drives a decision — keeping measurement separate from enforcement: the metric supplies evidence a validator may interpret and a gate may act on.
outcomes.anchor: 4.4 'Operate the Environment' — Ousterhout's measure-one-level-deeper paragraph + measurement/validator/gate role separation; re-homed from Operating MAGE in the Ch4/Ch5 merger.

outcomes.obj: a recurring procedure as engineering capital, distinguishing the knowledge a skill preserves from the authority only surrounding machinery carries
outcomes.statement: After this chapter, the reader can package a recurring procedure as a skill — the representations needed to reason about the work, the recurring decisions that matter, and a procedure for making them — and recognize that packaging preserves knowledge capital but does not by itself grant authority.
outcomes.anchor: 4.4 'Package Recurring Judgment' — a reusable skill needs three things; packaging does not itself enforce anything; re-homed from The Skills in the Ch4/Ch5 merger.

outcomes.obj: ex-ante obligations from ex-post ones and convert a recurring failure into the durable structure it was missing as engineering capital
outcomes.statement: After this chapter, the reader can split ex-ante obligations from ex-post ones, convert a recurring failure into the durable structure it was missing — a model, invariant, sensor, validator, or authority — as engineering capital, and place any obligation among residual, judgment-required, observed-only, or governed.
outcomes.anchor: point: a-governed-environment-grows-ex-ante-and-ex-post-with-conversion-the-hinge / the-conversion-lands-in-one-of-five-places / governance-conversion-forms-engineering-capital-the-positive-stock / where-a-goal-lands-turns-on-three-questions-starting-with-explicit-in-usable-form

outcomes.obj: why document accessibility is a hard, high-burden problem worth this machinery
outcomes.statement: After this chapter, the reader can explain the accessibility problem the case-study system solves and why a document is not just a file.
outcomes.anchor: Section titles 'a-noble-idea-with-a-crushing-implementation', 'the-rule-that-changed-the-burden', 'why-a-document-is-not-just-a-file'.

outcomes.obj: the project's stages to the kinds of work each demanded and the velocity each produced
outcomes.statement: After this chapter, the reader can map the case-study project's stages to the kinds of work each demanded and the velocity each produced.
outcomes.anchor: Section titles 'six-stages-then-a-seventh', 'velocity', 'the-kinds-of-work-it-required'.

outcomes.obj: how engineering failures leave behind several FORMS of durable capital — representation, decision rule, deterministic check, behavioral model, derived provenance, provisional measurement — some granted authority and some deliberately not, reading the case as evidence of mechanism and sequence rather than prevalence
outcomes.statement: After this chapter, the reader can trace how a failure becomes durable engineering capital (or deliberately remains provisional), distinguish the ex-post and ex-ante paths, and state what a single longitudinal case can and cannot establish.
outcomes.anchor: The eight episode sections under the standardized template ('The instruction satisfied to the letter' through 'Measurement: the story that stops before the gate', 6.4.1-6.4.8), the ex-ante confirmation 'Not every useful structure has an incident arc' (6.4.9), and the bounded epistemic close 'What this case supports' (6.4.10) in the chapter with identity label 'failures'.

outcomes.obj: how the built system forced the method out of it — the delegation staircase from solo co-coder to architect, each rung safe only because the step below minted the control it needed
outcomes.statement: After this chapter, the reader can trace the delegation staircase — co-coder, QA, review lead, tech lead, architect — by which the built system forced MAGE out of it, and can name why each rung was safe to climb only because the step below first minted the control that caught what the delegation dropped.
outcomes.anchor: The merged chapter: 'What ultimately got built' (six-responsibility tour + system-overview figure), 'The LLM as a function call' (#llm-as-function-call), and 'The staircase' with the five rung lead-ins (Co-coder / QA / Review lead / Tech lead / Architect) + the mage-staircase figure.

outcomes.obj: the convert-a-failure-into-a-mechanism move on two real incidents, using DocAble as the grounding case
outcomes.statement: After this chapter, the reader can recognize the convert-a-failure-into-a-mechanism move on two real incidents, using DocAble — what it does and how its six parts fit — as the grounding case.
outcomes.anchor: Section titles: 'two-birds-one-stone', 'the-shape-of-the-machine', 'two-scars', 'the-move-that-recurs'.

outcomes.obj: eight independently documented engineering systems as software factories under one consistent lens — what increased realization, what work inherits, what structures supervision, what stays human — without mistaking corroboration for a controlled test
outcomes.statement: After this chapter, the reader can analyze an independently documented engineering system as a software factory — apply the six-question lens, place its public evidence against the modeling ceiling, and state the common asymmetry the reports expose — without mistaking corroboration across reconstructions for a controlled test.
outcomes.anchor: The eight 'Inside X's Software Factory' mini-cases, the shared-baseline/differences section with the modeling-ceiling tiers, and the closing common-asymmetry diagnosis in the chapter with identity label 'mage-in-the-wild'.

outcomes.obj: the concurrency of a system with a synchronization model and formal invariant verification
outcomes.statement: After this chapter, the reader can model the process view — cataloging every lock in a synchronization model and backing its invariants with formal verification.
outcomes.anchor: Section titles 'formal-invariant-verification' + 'synchronization-model' (ts: 'A typed registry that models the system's synchronization behavior — every OS-level lock').

outcomes.obj: where a system runs with a deployment-topology model and an invariant-DAG execution policy
outcomes.statement: After this chapter, the reader can model the physical view — deployment topology and a typed deploy DAG — and name the one honest gap in the cost view.
outcomes.anchor: Section titles 'deployment-topology-model' + 'invariant-dag-execution-policy' + 'the-performance-cost-view-mostly-embodied-one-honest-gap'.

outcomes.obj: what the running system promises and the record it must leave behind
outcomes.statement: After this chapter, the reader can model an operating envelope — naming measured quantities and the bounds that drive admission or merely report — and derive an audit-grade changelog from a provenance record the code writes as it acts.
outcomes.anchor: Section titles 'what-the-system-promises-about-time-and-cost' + 'keeping-the-explanation-true-to-the-change' (operational-envelope-model + provenance-and-changelog-model).

outcomes.obj: a codebase's zones with a component & zone model and a rule-metadata registry
outcomes.statement: After this chapter, the reader can model the development view — every component's zone and the governance rules that ride it — as typed registries.
outcomes.anchor: Section titles 'component-zone-model' + 'rule-metadata-registry'; ts: 'A typed catalog of every component's code zone'.

outcomes.obj: a service-flow model and the domain registries it rests on
outcomes.statement: After this chapter, the reader can model the logical view as a structured service-flow model backed by frozen domain registries.
outcomes.anchor: Section titles 'service-flow-model' + 'domain-registries'; ts: 'The typed source-of-truth for a service-oriented architecture'.

outcomes.obj: why agreement is not correctness and place a mechanism at the earliest boundary where the obligation is legible and enforceable
outcomes.statement: After this chapter, the reader can explain why agreement is not correctness — authority needs an obligation independent of the work being judged — and place a mechanism at the earliest boundary where that obligation is legible and enforceable.
outcomes.anchor: point: enforcement-needs-an-independent-obligation-and-a-legible-boundary / a-drift-check-establishes-agreement-not-that-the-correspondence-is-right / place-enforcement-at-the-earliest-boundary-where-the-obligation-is-legible-and-decidable

outcomes.obj: the two engineering problems from the two properties of the agentic substrate
outcomes.statement: After this chapter, the reader can name the two properties of the agentic substrate — a finite, reconstructed reasoning state that meets a scale-driven locality problem, and probabilistic work that cannot certify itself but crosses an interposable, observable harness — and derive the two engineering problems, representation and enforcement, that follow, without treating either as a prerequisite of the other.
outcomes.anchor: Section titles: 'foundation-model-and-agentic-harness', 'the-reasoning-horizon', 'the-horizon-is-a-locality-problem', 'probabilistic-work-needs-external-authority', 'agentic-work-has-observable-seams'.

outcomes.obj: what the method changes for how software engineering is measured, staffed, and taught
outcomes.statement: After this chapter, the reader can evaluate the discipline-level implications: where judgment moved, what saturates, and why models are a common language of mature engineering.
outcomes.anchor: Section titles 'the-judgment-moved-and-it-moved-toward-you', 'what-this-changes-for-how-we-measure-staff-and-teach', 'models-are-the-universal-language-of-engineering'.

outcomes.statement: After this chapter, the reader can situate MAGE within the software-engineering literature — mechanized discipline (SE at Google), the design-pattern form (the Gang of Four), and the modeling tradition (MDSE) — as older aspirations under new economics.

outcomes.anchor: Section titles: 'The Engineering Object', 'an-open-ended-technology', 'whose-fault-is-it'.

outcomes.statement: After this chapter, the reader can explain the MAGE theory as a causal-loop dynamic model: its constructs, the four feedback dynamics, the seven hypotheses and two propositions, and the predictions and research agenda they imply.

outcomes.statement: After this chapter, the reader can govern accumulated control machinery through three views — a catalogue of what exists, an interaction graph of what collides over a shared resource, and a coverage relation of obligations against mechanisms — and grow, reconcile, and retire controls so the machinery stays coherent.
